metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after sharp spikes; reduce initial forecast peaks by 5–10%.
- After a price spike, model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward; apply a “cool-down” factor (e.g., reduce next 3–5 days’ forecast by 2–5% from peak).
- When sentiment is neutral or flat (all 0.00), model exhibits high variance and overconfidence; dampen forecast volatility by smoothing with 3-day moving average.
- Mean reversion is underutilized; if price deviates >15% from 30-day moving average, adjust forecast toward average with decay factor (e.g., 0.85 weight on prior avg).
- Forecast horizon 30d often misses short-term reversals; for days 1–7, apply 10–20% downward bias if recent 7-day avg is lower than 30-day avg.
- If true outcome shows “double dip” or “V-shaped” correction after spike, model tends to ignore the dip; add a 2–3 day lag correction to prevent premature recovery.
